feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
entry.summary: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.

entry.title: 'Bigger than Barack Obama's election': Scholars reflect on Mississippi Senate race
entry.summary: Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.

entry.title: The midterms were the largest win for either party in 50 years
entry.summary: Some 56% of people cast votes for Democrats in House races, compared to 42% who voted Republican. That 14-point spread is the widest win for either party in 50 years, since after Watergate.

entry.title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
entry.summary: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017.

entry.title: Anthropic raises more than $100B in IPO. And, Dems nominate Jeffries for House speaker
entry.summary: Despite growing concern over a possible AI bubble, Anthropic had a record-breaking initial public offering. And, Hakeem Jeffries could become the first Black Speaker of the House.

entry.title: Incoming House majority leader Katherine Clark stresses Democratic unity
entry.summary: As Democrats prepare to take control of the House, incoming majority leader Katherine Clark discusses the party's ambitious agenda and divisions within its ranks.

entry.title: Top House Democrat questions what Trump accomplished in Xi-Putin summit
entry.summary: Rep. Gregory Meeks raises concerns about U.S. alliances after Trump's summit with Xi and Putin. He also discusses Chinese espionage amid the Nvidia scandal.

entry.title: Ben Shapiro on conservative media and the future of the Republican Party
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep sits down with conservative commentator Ben Shapiro to discuss the future of the Republican party.

entry.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
entry.summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin have gathered in Shenzhen, China, for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.

entry.title: The law releasing the Epstein files passed one year ago. What do his victims say?
entry.summary: It's been a year since the House passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, forcing the Justice Department to release millions of files connected to the convicted sex offender. His victims speak out.
